'''Good Goods Pty. Ltd''',<ref name="GGPLOpenCorporates">{{Cite web |date=20 December 2011 |title=Good Goods Pty. Ltd. |url=https://opencorporates.com/companies/au/154870452 |access-date=7 January 2026 |website=[[OpenCorporates]]}}</ref> [[trading as]] '''Who Gives A Crap''' ('''WGAC'''), is a [[brand]] of [[toilet paper]], [[Tissue paper|tissues]], and [[paper towel]]s founded in Australia, and launched in 2012. The company sells recycled and bamboo products and donates half its profits to charity. Its products are manufactured in China.

== History ==
WGAC was founded by Simon Griffiths, Danny Alexander, and Jehan Ratnatunga.<ref name=":2">{{Cite news |last1=Macdonald |first1=Anthony |last2=Redrup |first2=Yolanda |date=24 August 2021 |title=Who Gives A Crap scores first big funding injection |work=Australian Financial Review |url=https://www.afr.com/street-talk/who-gives-a-crap-scores-first-big-funding-injection-20210824-p58lhi |access-date=2 March 2022}}</ref> Griffiths had the idea for the company after learning that more than 2 billion people didn't have access to a toilet.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=The irreverent toilet paper startup that cleaned up during the pandemic lockdown |url=https://fortune.com/2020/10/18/toilet-paper-sales-brands-pandemic-lockdown/ |access-date=2022-03-02 |website=Fortune |language=en}}</ref> WGAC launched in July 2012 with an [[Indiegogo]] crowdfunding campaign, for which Griffiths sat on a toilet in a warehouse for 50 hours, until the first $50,000 had been raised.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Nosowitz |first=Dan |date=2019-07-17 |title=What's the deal with all this fancy new toilet paper? |url=https://www.vox.com/the-goods/2019/7/17/20688093/toilet-paper-no-2-tushy-who-gives-a-crap-charmin |access-date=2022-03-02 |website=Vox |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite web |first1=Shubhangi |last1=Goel |first2=Karen |last2=Gilchrist |date=2021-10-07 |title=This CEO sat on a toilet for 50 hours to raise funds. Now, investors are giving him $30 million |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2021/10/07/this-ceo-sat-on-a-toilet-for-50-hours-to-raise-funds-for-sanitation.html |access-date=2022-03-02 |website=CNBC |language=en}}</ref> The first deliveries were made in March 2013.<ref name=":3" /> Since launching, Who Gives A Crap has donated over $13 million to Wateraid and other sanitation charities.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024 |title=Donations made |url=https://au.whogivesacrap.org/pages/our-impact  |website=Who Gives A Crap}}</ref>

By 2020, WGAC had grown to about 100 staff, and shipped products to 36 countries, with warehouses in [[Australia]], the [[United Kingdom]], the [[United States]], and the [[Netherlands]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Boddy |first=Natasha |date=29 December 2020 |title='I never meant to be a toilet paper mogul' Simon Griffiths |work=The Australian Financial Review |url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/2472986994 |access-date=2 March 2022|id={{ProQuest|2472986994}} }}</ref> The company began receiving investment funding in 2021, totalling around $50 million, from investors including [[Mike Cannon-Brookes]].<ref name=":2" /><ref>{{Cite news |last=Lynch |first=Jared |date=14 September 2021 |title=Who Gives A Crap flushed with $41m raising |work=The Australian |url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/2572064880 |access-date=2 March 2022|id={{ProQuest|2572064880}} }}</ref> WGAC is a [[B Corporation (certification)|certified B Corporation]], FSC certified, and ranked A in NRDC Sustainability denoting a commitment to positive social and environmental impact.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Burkhardt |first=Kai |date=2020-09-29 |title=Stay stocked up on toilet paper with these delivery services |url=https://www.cnn.com/2020/09/29/cnn-underscored/best-toilet-paper-delivery-service/index.html |access-date=2022-03-02 |website=CNN Underscored |language=en}}</ref>

During the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], especially in early 2020, there were [[Shortages related to the COVID-19 pandemic#Toilet paper and other paper products|numerous shortages]], including of toilet paper. In March 2020, WGAC received 30-40 times the typical number of daily sales, being forced to mark their online store as 'out of stock' for a short time - a waiting list began which grew to more than 500,000 people.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite news |last=Koziol |first=Michael |date=2 March 2022 |title=Sheet dreams are made of this for loo paper suppliers |work=The Sun-Herald |url=https://link.gale.com/apps/doc/A616577872/STND?u=wikipedia&sid=ebsco&xid=d6824817}}</ref>

== Products ==
WGAC toilet paper is created from [[Paper recycling|recycled paper]], and each roll is also individually wrapped in recycled paper. Since 2016, WGAC also sells toilet paper created from [[bamboo]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Henderson |first=Emma |date=2021-07-27 |title=Plastic Free July: Why we should all swap to this eco-friendly loo roll that helps to save trees |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/extras/indybest/house-garden/bathroom/recycled-toilet-paper-who-gives-a-crap-b1837676.html |access-date=2022-03-02 |website=The Independent |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Sirtori-Cortina |first=Daniela |date=2022-03-29 |title=The Battle for Your Toilet Paper Is On |language=en |work=Bloomberg.com |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/features/2022-03-29/bamboo-toilet-paper-softness-of-tree-free-eco-friendly-brands-are-improving |access-date=2022-05-01}}</ref> Its toilet paper products are manufactured in [[China]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wiggins |first=Jenny |date=2022-04-22 |title=Who gives a crap about the rising cost of toilet paper? |url=https://www.afr.com/companies/retail/who-gives-a-crap-about-the-rising-cost-of-toilet-paper-20220422-p5afcr |access-date=2022-05-01 |website=Australian Financial Review |language=en}}</ref> the United States, and the United Kingdom.

The company added garbage bags, food waste bags and dog poo bags to its product line in October 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Edwards |first=Aimee |date=2024-10-17 |title=Taking Out The Trash Has Never Looked So Good: Who Gives A Crap Adds Garbage Bags To Line |url=https://www.bandt.com.au/taking-out-the-trash-has-never-looked-so-good-who-gives-a-crap-adds-garbage-bags-to-line/ |access-date=2024-12-14 |website=B&T |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Charitable donations and partnerships ==
Half of the company's profits are donated to charities including [[WaterAid]], WaterSHED, and [[Shining Hope for Communities]].<ref name=":1" /> By 2024, WGAC had donated more than $13 million [[Australian dollar|AUD]], with $6 million USD resulting from the company's sales spike during 2020 pandemic shortages.<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":3" /><ref name="news">{{Cite web |last=Skantzos |first=Kathy |date=19 December 2020 |title=Who Gives a Crap gives away $5.85 million after exponential sales spike with pandemic |url=https://www.news.com.au/finance/business/retail/who-gives-a-crap-gives-away-585-million-after-exponential-sales-spike-with-pandemic/news-story/d7320db35c687332b957f0ba936d3e63 |access-date=2 May 2022 |website=News.com.au}}</ref>

By 2025, the company had donated £10m for projects such as Kenyan [[waterless toilet|waterless toilets]] and toilets in Timorese schools.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Butler |first=Sarah |date=2025-07-27 |title=On a roll: Who Gives a Crap toilet paper co-founder aims for 'world domination' |url=https://www.theguardian.com/business/2025/jul/27/who-gives-a-crap-toilet-paper-simon-griffiths-tesco-uk |access-date=2026-01-17 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref>

In March 2025, the company ended its partnership with influencer Lauren Dubois, due to differing views on the [[Gaza genocide]].<ref>{{cite web | title=Socialist responses to the Housing Crisis | date=21 March 2025 | url=https://www.3cr.org.au/greenleftradio/episode/socialist-responses-housing-crisis }}</ref> In May the same year, the company partnered with grocer [[Erewhon (store)|Erewhon]] to create limited edition "C.R.A.P" digestive smoothies.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Maguire |first=Lucy |date=2025-06-06 |title=The next wellness craze? Booty beauty |url=https://www.voguebusiness.com/story/beauty/the-next-wellness-craze-booty-beauty |access-date=2026-01-17 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20251108102820/https://www.vogue.com/article/the-next-wellness-craze-booty-beauty |archive-date=2025-11-08 |website=Vogue Business |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{cite press release | title=Erewhon and Eco-Friendly Toilet Paper Brand Who Gives a Crap Partner on the C.R.A.P. Smoothie to Encourage Healthy Poos | Novus Newswire | url=https://novusnewswire.com/erewhon-and-eco-friendly-toilet-paper-brand-who-gives-a-crap-partner-on-the-c-r-a-p-smoothie-to-encourage-healthy-poos/ }}</ref>
